text:
rachel: noticed a new CPU tail on streaming hosts during peak yesterday, ~+12% host CPU on parse/token path. anyone else see this?
tom: saw alerts, coincides with the mini-parser replay job we rolled at 03:05 UTC.
ivy: timeline? was anything else pushed to streaming pool?
rachel: only mini-parser-replay (small opt to reorder parse ops). spike started ~03:12 and was intermittent across ~25% of hosts.
kevin: pulled a quick perf snapshot from an affected host:
perf-sample:
assemble_normalize     29.4%
kvcache_lookup        15.0%
tokenize_stream       12.8%
grpc_read             9.1%
small_read_syscalls   5.2%
other                 28.5%

tom: tokenize_stream and assemble_normalize are big. suggests more prefix reparsing. did kvcache behavior change?
ivy: checking kvcache logs - small but noticeable drop in hit ratio during window: 99% -> 91% on affected hosts. looks like more unique prefixes.
kevin: traces show more fragmented emits from the parser; packetization changed so we now emit more micro-fragments when replay is active. those cause fresh prefix keys and more utf8-normalize calls.
rachel: repro command I used locally to mimic streaming with varied fragments:
```
./replay-hammer --model model-a --stream --clients 6 --msg-size=180 --fragment-mean=90 --duration=4m
```
tom: I ran that; can reproduce CPU tail on my devbox when replay is enabled. switching parser back to pre-replay ordering removes tail.
ivy: hypothesis: reorder changed parse assembly so sequence boundaries differ, reducing reuse in kvcache and increasing small grpc reads due to more chunk boundaries.
kevin: quick mitigations proposed: 1) revert mini-parser-replay on streaming pool 2) increase kvcache prefix TTL to 250ms on canary hosts 3) enable writev coalescing for reads (if possible) or reduce small-read syscall rate via socket buffering.
rachel: can we try TTL bump on a small canary group first?
tom: applying TTL bump to canary now, will report metrics in 5m.
ci-bot: Canary change applied: kvcache.prefix_ttl=250ms on streaming-canary-3/8
kevin: initial canary result: host CPU down ~6% and kvcache hit returned to ~95% on canary. good signal that prefix TTL helps.
ivy: longer-term fixes: 1) add tokenizer ascii fast-path to skip utf8-normalize when bytes are pure ASCII 2) add metric for fragment-size histogram + prefix reuse ratio so batcher/kernel changes can be judged for prefix impact 3) when rolling parser changes, run paired kvcache/batching canaries.
tom: i'll open PR to revert replay on streaming pool while we iterate. also will add a tracer flag when parser-replay is enabled so traces can be filtered easily.
rachel: kevin, can you prototype ascii fast-path? seems low-risk and high-reward.
kevin: will do. filing issue: ENGRT-7321 tokenizer: skip-normalize-if-ascii + unit tests.
ivy: follow-ups: tom to revert replay roll on streaming pool, kevin to PR ascii fast-path, rachel to keep kvcache telemetry for 24h, and add experiment checklist for parser/kernel/batcher interactions.
ci-bot: Rollback PR #732 -> merged by tom at 2026-05-04T04:45:12Z
rachel: thanks all. schedule short postmortem and add the fragment/prefix telemetry work item to next sprint. :thumbsup:
